response.reason: NL1 establishes a root-level initial entry into Operate on power-on and an owner-local transition capability among Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking substates of Operate. NL2 gives the explicit start/keyOff signals as transition endpoints at the root scope (power on -> Operate, Operate -> off/terminated by keyOff). NL3 restates that within Operate the substates transition based on accelerating/braking/stopping actions, which is context reinforcing NL1's transition group with named guard/event concepts (accelerating, braking, stopping) rather than a new structural obligation, but it does add containment obligations for the four substates under Operate and an event-consumer-style restatement; I treat NL3 as context because NL1 already covers the grouping and containment; however per instructions I must still emit at least one contract for NL3 to mark it covered without duplicating. I add a state_action-adjacent note: NL3 doesn't state continuous action, only substate transition based on actions, so no new state_action contract. I extract: (1) NL1 initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (2) NL1 containment Operate contains Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking (four containment contracts); (3) NL1 transition_groups for Operate-local substate transitions among Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking (established as mutually reachable substates, but exact source/target pairs are not individually stated beyond "transitions between" - so I create a transition_groups entry with Idle as anchor source and Accelerating/Cruising/Braking as alternatives, and also the reverse since discourse says "transitions between" implying bidirectionality; I add endpoint contracts for the bidirectional pairs actually stated: since NL1 only says "transitions between X, Y, and Z" without specific pairs, I preserve this as a transition_groups relation with Idle as source and other three as alternatives, then a second group with each of those as source back to Idle, reflecting the bidirectional generic reading, and separate endpoint contracts are not manufactured beyond what discourse states); (4) NL2 root-level transition endpoints: start signal power-on entry (already covered by initial_entry) and keyOff signal transition from Operate to an off/terminated target - I treat this as termination since keyOff turns the system off, with a termination contract for Operate->off via keyOff; but NL2 explicitly frames start as turning on (entry trigger) and keyOff as turning off (exit trigger), so I create two transition-endpoint-style contracts: an initial_entry-adjacent trigger_set for start attached to root initial edge, and a termination contract for Operate-scope termination via keyOff. (5) NL3 marks covered via containment contracts restated and a trigger_set contract capturing accelerating/braking/stopping as event concepts governing the local transition group, satisfying the "must retain at least one contract with that segment_id" rule.

NL2 gives the explicit start/keyOff signals as transition endpoints at the root scope (power on -> Operate, Operate -> off/terminated by keyOff). NL3 restates that within Operate the substates transition based on accelerating/braking/stopping actions, which is context reinforcing NL1's transition group with named guard/event concepts (accelerating, braking, stopping) rather than a new structural obligation, but it does add containment obligations for the four substates under Operate and an event-consumer-style restatement; I treat NL3 as context because NL1 already covers the grouping and containment; however per instructions I must still emit at least one contract for NL3 to mark it covered without duplicating. I add a state_action-adjacent note: NL3 doesn't state continuous action, only substate transition based on actions, so no new state_action contract. I extract: (1) NL1 initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (2) NL1 containment Operate contains Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking (four containment contracts); (3) NL1 transition_groups for Operate-local substate transitions among Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking (established as mutually reachable substates, but exact source/target pairs are not individually stated beyond "transitions between" - so I create a transition_groups entry with Idle as anchor source and Accelerating/Cruising/Braking as alternatives, and also the reverse since discourse says "transitions between" implying bidirectionality; I add endpoint contracts for the bidirectional pairs actually stated: since NL1 only says "transitions between X, Y, and Z" without specific pairs, I preserve this as a transition_groups relation with Idle as source and other three as alternatives, then a second group with each of those as source back to Idle, reflecting the bidirectional generic reading, and separate endpoint contracts are not manufactured beyond what discourse states); (4) NL2 root-level transition endpoints: start signal power-on entry (already covered by initial_entry) and keyOff signal transition from Operate to an off/terminated target - I treat this as termination since keyOff turns the system off, with a termination contract for Operate->off via keyOff; but NL2 explicitly frames start as turning on (entry trigger) and keyOff as turning off (exit trigger), so I create two transition-endpoint-style contracts: an initial_entry-adjacent trigger_set for start attached to root initial edge, and a termination contract for Operate-scope termination via keyOff. This is a scoped initial-entry mismatch. (2) Containment contracts NL1-CONTAIN-1..4 are satisfied: Idle, AcceleratingOrCruising(bound to 'Accelerating'/'Cruising' NL names), and Braking are exact children of Operate in both source and model, so they are omitted. (3) NL1-ENDPOINT-ACCEL/CRUISE/BRAKE and the derived Accelerating->Cruising contract require author-source-local endpoints Idle->Accelerating, Idle->Cruising, Idle->Braking, and Accelerating->Cruising. The exact source/model only realizes a single merged state 'AcceleratingOrCruising' representing both 'Accelerating' and 'Cruising' as one node, and the complete transition inventory has no edge distinguishing Accelerating from Cruising, so the Idle->Cruising and Accelerating->Cruising obligations are not realized as distinct edges; only one merged Idle<->AcceleratingOrCruising edge exists. stage_receipts.reason: NL1 establishes a root-level initial entry into Operate on power-on and an owner-local transition capability among Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking substates of Operate. NL2 gives the explicit start/keyOff signals as transition endpoints at the root scope (power on -> Operate, Operate -> off/terminated by keyOff). NL3 restates that within Operate the substates transition based on accelerating/braking/stopping actions, which is context reinforcing NL1's transition group with named guard/event concepts (accelerating, braking, stopping) rather than a new structural obligation, but it does add containment obligations for the four substates under Operate and an event-consumer-style restatement; I treat NL3 as context because NL1 already covers the grouping and containment; however per instructions I must still emit at least one contract for NL3 to mark it covered without duplicating. I add a state_action-adjacent note: NL3 doesn't state continuous action, only substate transition based on actions, so no new state_action contract. I extract: (1) NL1 initial_entry root->Operate on power-on; (2) NL1 containment Operate contains Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking (four containment contracts); (3) NL1 transition_groups for Operate-local substate transitions among Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking (established as mutually reachable substates, but exact source/target pairs are not individually stated beyond "transitions between" - so I create a transition_groups entry with Idle as anchor source and Accelerating/Cruising/Braking as alternatives, and also the reverse since discourse says "transitions between" implying bidirectionality; I add endpoint contracts for the bidirectional pairs actually stated: since NL1 only says "transitions between X, Y, and Z" without specific pairs, I preserve this as a transition_groups relation with Idle as source and other three as alternatives, then a second group with each of those as source back to Idle, reflecting the bidirectional generic reading, and separate endpoint contracts are not manufactured beyond what discourse states); (4) NL2 root-level transition endpoints: start signal power-on entry (already covered by initial_entry) and keyOff signal transition from Operate to an off/terminated target - I treat this as termination since keyOff turns the system off, with a termination contract for Operate->off via keyOff; but NL2 explicitly frames start as turning on (entry trigger) and keyOff as turning off (exit trigger), so I create two transition-endpoint-style contracts: an initial_entry-adjacent trigger_set for start attached to root initial edge, and a termination contract for Operate-scope termination via keyOff. (5) NL3 marks covered via containment contracts restated and a trigger_set contract capturing accelerating/braking/stopping as event concepts governing the local transition group, satisfying the "must retain at least one contract with that segment_id" rule.
